title: Oscillations and Simple Harmonic Motion

cards.h: Everything that swings, hums or ticks
cards.b:
A child on a swing, a plucked guitar string, a clock pendulum, atoms in a crystal, a bridge in the wind. Countless systems wobble back and forth around a resting position.

The simplest, and the most important, kind of wobble is simple harmonic motion (SHM). Once you understand it, you understand the heart of sound, light, radio, quantum physics and clocks.

SHM happens when a force pulls an object back toward the centre, and the pull grows in proportion to how far it has been pushed away. Hooke's law for a spring:

Hooke's law

F = - k x

x is the displacement; k is the stiffness (N/m); the minus sign says the force opposes the displacement. Stretch right, it pulls left. Pass the centre, it pulls the other way. The result is endless oscillation.

Amplitude (A) is the largest distance from the centre. Period (T) is the time for one full cycle. Frequency (f) is cycles per second, in hertz (Hz).

Link

f = 1 / T

If one swing takes 2 s, the frequency is 0.5 Hz. Plotted against time, the position makes a smooth wave called a sine curve.

Period formulas

Mass on a spring: T = 2 pi x square root of (m / k)
Simple pendulum: T = 2 pi x square root of (L / g)

A heavier mass on a spring swings more slowly; a stiffer spring swings faster. For the pendulum, only the length and g matter. The mass of the bob does not enter, and (for small swings) neither does the amplitude.

Galileo noticed this around 1583 watching a swinging lamp, and Huygens used it to build the first accurate pendulum clock in 1656.

At the ends of the swing the object stops for an instant: all its energy is potential (stored). At the centre it moves fastest: all energy is kinetic. In between the energy is shared.

The total, (1/2) k A squared, stays constant if there is no friction. In real life, damping slowly drains the energy as heat, and oscillations die away unless you keep pushing, as a parent does to a swing.

cards.h: Resonance: pushing at the right rhythm
cards.b:
Every oscillator has a natural frequency. If you drive it at that frequency, even gentle pushes add up and the amplitude grows enormously. This is resonance.

It is how a child gets higher on a swing, how a radio tunes to a station, and how a singer can shatter a glass. It can also destroy: the Tacoma Narrows Bridge in the USA twisted apart in wind in 1940. Soldiers break step on bridges for the same reason.

Pendulum of length 1 m: T = 2 pi x square root of (1/9.8) = 6.28 x 0.32 = 2.0 s. A 'seconds pendulum' takes one second per swing, so its full period is 2 s, with length close to one metre.

Spring with m = 0.5 kg and k = 200 N/m: T = 6.28 x square root of (0.5/200) = 6.28 x 0.05 = 0.31 s, so f is about 3.2 Hz.

On the Moon (g about 1.6) the same pendulum would take 2 pi x square root of (1/1.6) = 4.9 s: slower.

• 'A heavier pendulum swings slower.' Not so; mass cancels out for a pendulum.
  • 'Acceleration is zero at the ends.' It is largest at the ends, where the restoring force is biggest. It is zero at the centre.
  • 'Bigger swing, longer period.' For small swings, the period does not depend on amplitude.

C. V. Raman studied the vibrations of Indian drums and strings. In the 1920s he showed that the tabla and mridangam produce nearly harmonic overtones, because of the loaded circle of paste on the drum skin. That is why these instruments sound so tuneful, unlike most drums.

The sitar, tanpura and veena also rely on string vibration and resonance of their hollow gourds. Raman received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930 for a different discovery, on light scattering.

• SHM arises when the restoring force is proportional to displacement: F = -kx.
  • Period T = 2 pi x square root of (m/k) for a spring; T = 2 pi x square root of (L/g) for a pendulum.
  • Frequency f = 1/T, measured in hertz.
  • Energy swaps between kinetic and potential; resonance builds large oscillations.

Think about it

1. Why would a grandfather clock run slow at the top of a high mountain?
2. Why do marching soldiers break step crossing a bridge?
